passage: Yogesh, you look like Nikhil did at your age: phone in hand, guilt on the face. Let me tell you what I did. I once locked all my apps from nine to six, because games were eating my life. For three days I felt strong. On the fourth day my manager needed a file and my work chat was locked. I broke the lock in a panic and dropped the whole thing for a month. Then I sat down and asked: what was working? The evening games block was working. What was not? Blocking the work apps. So I made the rule smaller: games locked from six to eleven at night, work apps free at all times. It still holds two years later.

qa.a: Games are locked from six to eleven at night.

passage: Jomon's first attempt had been a disaster: a total app lock that stopped him from answering his manager and ended with him deleting the whole thing. This time he had one more problem. He had just started night-shift support at a call centre in Kochi, so "evening" meant something different for him. He sat with a notebook and thought about which parts had actually helped. Blocking games at night: that had helped; he'd slept better. The daytime block on work chat: that had hurt. So he set a new rule. Games blocked for four hours before each shift and during it, work apps always open. His teammate Bhupen, who had watched the first attempt collapse, asked, "Still locked out of everything?" Jomon laughed. "Only the fun stuff. I kept the part that worked."

qa.a: At a call centre in Kochi.

qa.q: How did Jomon feel about his first attempt?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed by how it had collapsed, but calm enough to sort out which parts helped.

qa.q: What makes Jomon's new rule better than the first one?
qa.a: It keeps the block on games, which helped his sleep, and keeps work apps open, so the rule supports his goal instead of fighting his job.

qa.a: Bhupen, who watched the first attempt fail, is likely amused and relieved to see a gentler rule that could last.

passage: In his flat in Gurugram, Mohit reopened the blocker app he had deleted a week ago in a panic. His colleague Afreen, visiting to work on their joint presentation, peered at the screen. "Round two?" "Round two, smarter." He talked it through as he set it up. "Last time I blocked everything all day. Work chat, email, maps, even the bank. Of course I broke it by noon." He tapped the settings. "What actually helped was evenings without games. I finished two books that week." So he set it: games and video apps blocked from eight to eleven every night; work apps never blocked. Afreen nodded. "That's a rule you might keep." A month later, the block was still there, and Mohit had finished four more books.

qa.q: Which apps did Mohit block from eight to eleven?
qa.a: Games and video apps, every night.

qa.q: How did Mohit feel setting the blocker up again?
qa.a: He felt hopeful and a bit wiser, calling it round two, smarter, after the first panic.

qa.q: What else could Mohit adjust if evenings get busy with work?
qa.a: Shift the game block to another quiet time and keep work apps open, so the rule still fits his day.

qa.a: Afreen seems amused but encouraging, thinking this rule is one he might actually keep.
